Boyle, who directed O’Connell in The Sun newspaper movie Ink , was speaking on the Alchemy with Anthony Mason podcast when he made the comment. The conversation turned to the skills of O’Connell and Robert Pattinson , the new James Bond , prompting Boyle to discuss the next 007 movie. “Jack O’Connell would have been a great Bond as well,” he said. “I can see they’re beginning in all this talk they’re talking about Jack O’Connell as a possible villain,” he added, approving of the idea. He added Pattinson and O’Connell had similar screen magnetism. “They have that thing – you want to watch them,” he said. “It’s impossible to quantify what it is, otherwise we’d all buy it for ourselves, but it’s just there and you want to follow them.” Watch on Deadline There were some rumors that O’Connell was among those considered for the plum role before Twilight and Dune star Pattinson was selected by Amazon. title: Matt Damon Narrates Ford Racing’s ‘Go Like Hell’ Thanksgiving Day Ad Directed by Zack Snyder
full_text: × Nov 26, 2026 10:00am PT Matt Damon Narrates Ford Racing’s ‘Go Like Hell’ Thanksgiving Day Ad Directed by Zack Snyder By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Matt Damon Narrates Ford Racing’s ‘Go Like Hell’ Thanksgiving Day Ad Directed by Zack Snyder 31 minutes ago Tony Romo, After Parting Ways With CBS Sports, Named ‘Chief Predictions Officer’ of Jake Paul’s Betr Betting App 21 hours ago Hallmark’s New Podcast Push Kicks Off With Interview Series Hosted by Melissa Peterman That ‘Breaks the Fourth Wall,’ With More Shows to Come 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ford Racing Ford Racing tapped Matt Damon , star of “Ford v Ferrari,” to introduce the all-new Ford GT41 Hypercar in a new ad directed by filmmaker Zack Snyder. The ad is slated to air during CBS’s broadcast of the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears Thanksgiving Day NFL game, which starts at 1 p.m. ET. The 90-second spot centers on the GT41 Hypercar and the U.S. automaker’s return to the top class of the FIA World Endurance Championship and Le Mans in 2027 — and evoking Damon’s turn as a driver in “Ford v Ferrari.” The ad was produced by Artists Equity, the studio led by Damon and Ben Affleck. ( Watch the full spot below. ) Related Stories Chris Pratt to Star in Sci-Fi Family Drama 'The Traveler,' Inks First-Look Producing Deal at Paramount (EXCLUSIVE) Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' Comeback: A Smaller $5 Million Salary, Optimistic Theater Owners and More “What does it mean to be American?” Damon says in the ad. “Well, many things to many people. To us, it’s not just where we hang our hat. It’s downright relentless grit.” The spot ends with Damon praising Ford Racing fans: “More than part of the team, you’re our fuel. Why we persevere. Every mile feeds the next. Because that’s what it means to be American. That we always — without fail — go like hell.” The spot chronicles the journey of Ford’s GT41 Hypercar from the U.S. to the legendary Circuit de la Sarthe in Le Mans, France, ahead of its competitive debut in 2027. The film was shot in and around Los Angeles, symbolizing “Ford Racing’s return to the scene of some of its greatest motorsport triumphs,” according to the car company. It also features connections to “Ford v Ferrari”: For example, the airplane hangar used to load the GT41’s shipping container is the same one used for the Ford GT40 race workshop in the movie. Damon, who serves as chief content officer of Artists Equity, portrayed Ford driver Carroll Shelby in 2019’s “Ford v Ferrari.” “Telling the story of Le Mans ‘66 [in ‘Ford v Ferrari’] was one of the highlights of my career, so getting to lend my voice to the next chapter felt very full circle,” Damon said in a statement. “Revisiting this one with Ford and Zack, as they take on the world’s toughest racing all over again, was a real privilege.” Snyder, known for films including “300,” “Watchmen” and “Justice League,” commented: “The amazing part about getting a chance to work on this ‘Go Like Hell’ spot for Ford Racing was the chance to mix the nostalgia of the ’66 GT40 with this modern hypercar and its incredible engineering as well as this narrative that follows the transporting of the car across America.” The ad coincides with Thursday’s official public unveiling of the Ford GT41 at Detroit’s Ford Field. The new vehicle takes its name from the Ford GT40, which secured four consecutive overall victories at Le Mans between 1966 and 1969. Like its predecessor, the GT41’s name reflects its dimensions, standing 41 inches from the ground to the air intake. The Ford GT41 will make its competitive debut in the 2027 FIA World Endurance Championship, with the season opening in Qatar in March before the team heads to Le Mans in June. title: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Devouring $85M Over Thanksgiving Weekend as ‘Focker-in-Law,’ ‘Hexed’ Launch
full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All November 26, 2026 9:51am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Joseph Zada in 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.' Courtesy of Everett Collection Logo text The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is claiming the head of the table at the Thanksgiving weekend box office as Focker-in-Law and Hexed enter the arena. Lionsgate’s sixth film in the dystopian Hunger Games franchise screens in 4,018 North American theaters for its sophomore frame, as it grossed around $15.1 million on Wednesday. Director Francis Lawrence’ s adaptation of author Suzanne Collins’ 2025 prequel novel is looking at a five-day sum around $85 million to take its domestic cume to roughly $233 million through Sunday. The movie stars Joseph Zada as a young Haymitch Abernathy, played by Woody Harrelson in the first four Jennifer Lawrence-led films. Related Stories Movies Scott Caan Thought He Got a Prank Text. It Was Actually David Fincher Wanting Him in 'Cliff Booth' Movies 'Avengers: Doomsday' Eyes $270M Opening as 'Dune: Part Three' Also Heads for Big Start After opening to the fifth-biggest launch in Lionsgate history last weekend with $119 million domestically and $225 million worldwide, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping has continued its momentum. The $150 million-budgeted film, which earned an A- CinemaScore, grossed $15.98 million domestically on Tuesday to notch the franchise’s biggest first Tuesday, narrowly topping the $15.96 million for 2013’s Catching Fire . Sunrise’ s Monday sum of $12.8 million also bested the series’ previous top opening Monday of $12.3 million for Catching Fire . The East Coast has been impacted by a major storm stretching from the Midwest to the Eastern seaboard, leading the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to be moved to Saturday for the first postponement in its 100-year history. The inclement weather could slow down moviegoing throughout the weekend, including on Black Friday, which tends to be the biggest day for the box office over the Thanksgiving frame. Disney released Hexed in 3,725 North American theaters on Wednesday, with the animated fantasy film collecting an estimated $7.6 million on opening day, including $2.1 million in Tuesday previews. Directors Jason Hand and Fawn Veerasunthorn’s movie, which carries a budget north of $200 million, could be heading for a five-day launch around $35 million. This looks to be down a bit from the $45 million opening that the studio had initially been projecting . Hexed Disney Enterprises, Inc. Hailee Steinfeld, Rashida Jones and Jodie Foster lead the voice cast for Hexed , which centers on a mother and her teenage daughter grappling with the girl’s magical powers. The studio has been hopeful that it will continue to run throughout the holiday corridor and follow the lead of this year’s original animated features with pleasing performances, including Goat and Hoppers , although other recent originals like Forgotten Island have struggled. Earning an A- CinemaScore, Hexed holds a 66 percent critics score on Rotten Tomatoes. The Hollywood Reporter critic Angie Han wrote in her review that it offers “more than enough to make for a pleasurably transportive trip to the theater.” Universal Pictures’ Meet the Parents sequel Focker-in-Law launched in 3,382 North American theaters on Wednesday, grossing $5.3 million on its opening day. Director John Hamburg’s film appears to be in line for a $36.3 million opening over the five-day frame, also a bit below the initial projection in the $45 million range. Ariana Grande joins franchise returnees Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro, as she plays a woman set to marry the son of Stiller’s Greg Focker. Ben Stiller (left) and Ariana Grande in Focker-in-Law. Universal and Paramount Meet the Parents opened to $28.6 million domestically in 2000 (en route to its $166.2 million domestic cume). Sequel Meet the Fockers launched even bigger with $70.5 million over the five-day Christmas frame in 2004, while 2010’s Little Fockers dropped to $45 million for its five-day opening frame. Focker-in-Law earned a B+ CinemaScore from audiences and holds a rough 29 percent critical score on Rotten Tomatoes. In his review for THR , critic Frank Scheck wrote that the sequel “feels like the nadir in a series that recycles the same tired jokes in increasingly desperate manner.” Disney animated features are known for debuting over Thanksgiving, as Moana 2 opened to a massive $225 million over the five-day weekend in 2024 to help that year’s holiday frame set the all-time record with $423 million across all titles. Last year, Zootopia 2 launched on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving and collected $158 million over the five days to help lead the frame to a combined sum of $290 million. The total for this year’s holiday frame is expected to rank below both of those. In limited release, Netflix launched director David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth on 252 Imax screens in North America. The Brad Pitt-led follow-up to 2019’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood appears headed for around $5 million domestically over the five days before it begins streaming Dec. 23. THR

title: BBC’s Antisemitism Crisis Represents an Unprecedented Chapter for the World’s Most Trusted News Organization
full_text: × Nov 26, 2026 9:29am PT BBC’s Antisemitism Crisis Represents an Unprecedented Chapter for the World’s Most Trusted News Organization By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest BBC Set to Be Investigated Over Antisemitism as Former Producer Says: ‘It Is a Hostile Environment for Jews Who Want to Be Openly Jewish’ 6 hours ago ‘Pirates of the Caribbean’ Secret Cinema Immersive Stage Show Teases Behind-the-Scenes Rehearsal Footage (EXCLUSIVE) 8 hours ago Former Disney Boss Bob Iger ‘Got ABC Employee Pregnant’ During Affair, New Book Claims 8 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images It is a dark day for the BBC . On Thursday, government adviser Lord John Mann announced he is launching an investigation into alleged antisemitism at the broadcaster. It is an unprecedented chapter for the corporation, long held up as one of the most venerable and reliable media institutions in the world. For those who have been paying attention, however, the move is not surprising following a litany of public missteps dating as far back as 2021, when BBC News misreported an incident in which a group of Jewish students were attacked on a bus in Central London and then doubled down on it, despite eventually acknowledging the reporting lacked accuracy and impartiality. Related Stories Chris Pratt to Star in Sci-Fi Family Drama 'The Traveler,' Inks First-Look Producing Deal at Paramount (EXCLUSIVE) Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' Comeback: A Smaller $5 Million Salary, Optimistic Theater Owners and More Later, the broadcaster steadfastly refused to reprimand Gary Lineker, one of its most high-profile sports anchors, as he repeatedly breached its much-touted social media guidelines, which were instituted precisely because of Lineker’s increasingly political Twitter activity. Under the guidelines, high-profile presenters hosting flagship programs are expected to be impartial while the show is on air and for a two-week window before and after. At the time, he called the guidelines “very sensible.” It was only when last year Lineker reposted an Instagram story about “Zionists” alongside a rat emoji that the BBC finally cut him loose. Even then, rather than a punitive measure, his exit was presented to the public as a mutually agreed decision for the host to leave after the final “Match of the Day” episode aired the following week. The BBC’s press release went on to call him a “defining voice in football coverage” and “thank him for the contribution he has made.” Critics compared the BBC’s apparently favorable treatment of Lineker to that of former BBC Radio 5 Live broadcaster Danny Baker, who was sacked immediately in 2019 after tweeting an image of a chimpanzee with the caption “Royal baby leaves hospital” just days after Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, gave birth, with the BBC calling it a “serious error of judgment.” The following month saw yet another incident when the BBC broadcast a little-known rapper’s rant about a former (apparently Jewish) boss , described alternately as a “fucking Zionist” and “bald-headed cunt,” before the crowd was engaged in a chant of “Death to the IDF.” It later emerged that producers had assessed the rapper as “high risk” and yet decided to broadcast his set live. Even as he embarked on his rant, which BBC chair Samir Shah later acknowledged consisted of “unconscionable antisemitic views,” no one at the broadcaster thought to cut the Glastonbury feed. Shah apologized for the oversight, and the BBC’s director of music, Lorna Clarke, briefly “stepped back” from her duties, although it appears little other action was taken (she has long since returned to her post). Then, last month, it was revealed that the BBC had reached an out-of-court settlement with one of its top factual producers, Lucie Kon, after she brought a legal claim alleging antisemitic discrimination. Kon, an Emmy and Oscar winner who exec produced “Mr Nobody Against Putin,” had worked for the corporation for 25 years but said that after Oct. 7, when Hamas murdered 1,200 people in Israel and kidnapped 250 more, the atmosphere toward her changed. The BBC rejected those claims but agreed to pay Kon £400,000 ($520,000) to settle out of court. For health reasons, Kon accepted. By comparison, the average award handed down by courts for race discrimination in the U.K. is £29,532, according to the most recent statistics. At the same time, the BBC’s reporting on Israel has been an ongoing source of contention. There was the Gaza documentary which failed to tell viewers the narrator was the son of a senior Hamas official , the report speculating Israel had bombed a hospital in Gaza which had actually been hit by a Hamas rocket misfiring and the news story in which an anchor misrepresented a Reuters story , saying the IDF was “targeting … medical teams as well as Arabic speakers” when in fact the medical teams and Arabic speakers were part of the IDF, there to assess patients on the ground. A leaked internal report last year — the same one that led to BBC boss Tim Davie resigning when it revealed the BBC had doctored one of President Trump’s speeches — noted that BBC Arabic, a part of the corporation’s World Service, had made 215 corrections and clarifications in its reporting of the Israel-Gaza war since 2023, amounting to two a week. At the time, a BBC spokesperson told Variety : “BBC News Arabic strives for the highest standards of journalism across its services.” (Incidentally, the BBC World Service currently operates in 45 languages, including Arabic, Amharic, English, Hausa, Kirundi, Marathi, Tigrinya, Ukrainian, Urdu and Yoruba. It does not include Hebrew.) So how did the BBC find itself embroiled in yet another crisis? Part of the problem stems from the fact that the corporation effectively marks its own homework. While British newspapers are regulated by an independent body, IPSO, the BBC operates the Executive Complaints Unit to investigate grievances about itself. But there is also a sense that the BBC, even under its new director general Matt Brittin, is not interested in engaging seriously with the issue. Each time there is a public blunder, the BBC will roll out the same playbook: issue a cut-and-paste apology (usually with reluctance), defend its reporting and make a gesture to suggest it has learned a lesson. But the sheer frequency of incidents — only a handful of which even spin out into the public realm — suggests nothing is being learned. Earlier this month, the corporation’s deputy director-general, Rhodri Talfan Davies, was asked during an on-the-record Q&A session with journalists whether he would support an internal inquiry into antisemitism at the BBC. His response was to deny there was a “deep-rooted issue” or any “institutional discrimination” at the broadcaster. Notably, he didn’t answer the second part of the journalist’s question, namely, if Talfan Davies didn’t think there was antisemitism at the BBC, “why do you think many of your Jewish employees think there is?” Even the corporation’s checkbox response to Lord Mann’s announcement on Thursday gives the impression, whether intended or not, that the threat of an investigation into its internal conduct is of little consequence. When approached for comment, a BBC publicist told Variety by email, “We’d also like to direct you to the below statement, that we’ve previously issued,” before literally copy-and-pasting it underneath. In his speech announcing the investigation, Lord Mann said he is “not interested in targeting individuals. That would entirely miss the point. I am targeting the institution.” The biggest clue as to the depth of the BBC’s antisemitism problem will be whether the institution even cares. title: Scott Caan Is “100 Percent” Open to Reprising Role in ‘Ocean’s 14’ With Casey Affleck
full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All November 26, 2026 9:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Scott Caan and Casey Affleck in 'Ocean's Eleven.' Everett If it’s up to Scott Caan and Casey Affleck , the Malloy brothers, aka “Mormon twins,” will be returning in Ocean’s 14 . While recently chatting with The Hollywood Reporter about his new movie The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , Caan was happy to share he and Affleck are “100 percent” open to reprising Turk and Virgil Malloy, respectively, in the follow-up that’s in development at Warner Bros. “If the movie gets made, I’m 100 percent in. I actually have not read the script yet, but I hear the script is great,” he said, adding, “I just saw Casey the other night too, and I asked him and he was like, ‘Yeah, let’s go.’ So I can speak for Casey. We’re in if it happens.” Related Stories Movies Scott Caan Thought He Got a Prank Text. It Was Actually David Fincher Wanting Him in 'Cliff Booth' Movies 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth' Review: Brad Pitt, David Fincher and Quentin Tarantino Mix a Cool Cocktail in Free-Flowing Spinoff THR has reached out to Warner Bros. for comment. Caan and Affleck first appeared in 2001’s Ocean’s Eleven , playing two bickering brothers that Danny Ocean (George Clooney) and Rusty Ryan (Brad Pitt) recruited from Utah to serve as the crew’s getaway drivers and mechanics. The pair reprised their roles in 2004’s Ocean’s Twelve and 2007’s Ocean’s Thirteen . David Leitch ( John Wick and The Fall Guy ) is attached to direct the latest installment in the heist movie franchise that is also expected to see Clooney, Pitt, Matt Damon, Julia Roberts and Don Cheadle return. “Working with those guys, I got so spoiled,” Caan recalled of previously working with the stacked cast and filmmaker Steven Soderbergh. “I was young and I’m like, ‘Oh, this is what making big movies is,’ and it isn’t always like that. I remember walking into a room with all those guys thinking like, ‘All right, where’s the bad guy going to be or the guy who’s no fun?’ And I learned very quickly in my early 20s [that] the most talented people are always the coolest people and the nicest people.” He added, “So if they called me right now and said, ‘We’re going to make 10 more of those movies,’ I would sign up having not read any of the scripts. That’s how much I like all those people.” Ocean’s 14 is expected to begin filming in late 2027. Leitch recently told People that “everybody’s excited about moving it forward,” but that “getting all those people together, and their schedules are always the issue.” THR

title: Mark Tildesley Dies: ‘No Time to Die’, ‘F1: The Movie’ & London Olympics Production Designer Was 63
full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Former NBA Champ David M. Tildesley’s many credits include James Bond movie No Time To Die , 28 Days Later , The Constant Gardener , The Two Popes , Jay Kelly , Joseph Kosinski’s F1: The Movie , and Sam Mendes’ upcoming Beatles movies. Mendes today described his collaborator as “entirely original and extraordinarily gifted”. Tildesley’s career spanned more than three decades and he collaborated with leading filmmakers including Danny Boyle, Richard Curtis, Michael Winterbottom, Martin McDonagh, Mike Leigh, Paul Thomas Anderson, Cary Joji Fukunaga, Ron Howard, Ben Wheatley, Oliver Stone and Mendes. He won three British Film Designers Guild awards, for High-Rise, Empire of Light and F1: The Movie , as well as a Set Decorators Society of America prize, an Art Directors Guild award, and a British Independent Film Award. Mendes said today: “Mark was a one-off: gentle, funny, warm, mischievous, entirely original and extraordinarily gifted. My abiding memory of him is from Empire of Light , flying down the Margate seafront on a motorised scooter, his technicolored scarf flapping in the wind, twinkling like a schoolboy playing hooky. A unique spirit and a wonderful artist. I am one of hundreds of people who are desperately sad that he is gone.” The British Film Designers Guild (BFDG) said: “We are very sad to hear the news of Mark’s death. title: Record Store Day Co-Founder on How Black Friday Evolved Into a Major Holiday for Vinyl Hounds, and What Will Fly Off the Shelves This Year
full_text: × Nov 26, 2026 8:43am PT Record Store Day Co-Founder on How Black Friday Evolved Into a Major Holiday for Vinyl Hounds, and What Will Fly Off the Shelves This Year The biggest shopping day of the year isn't just for big-box stores. Michael Kurtz predicts which artists, from Noah Kahan to the Beatles, will have LP enthusiasts up and in the shops early By Andrea Dresdale Plus Icon Andrea Dresdale Latest See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Record Store Day In April of this year, the 19th installment of Record Store Day was the event’s most successful ever, but Nov. 27 brings another opportunity for music junkies to get their vinyl on: Record Store Day Black Friday . While the O.G. Record Store Day was conceived as a general celebration of independent record stores, and features limited-edition, in-store only releases, the Black Friday edition exists for a different reason: to give those indie stores a slice of the “biggest shopping day of the year” pie. That’s also why the vinyl releases you’ll find making their debuts on Black Friday are more likely to remain there for the rest of the holiday season, and why many stores will make them available on their websites starting on Saturday the 28th. The concept of hyping local independent record stores as a must for holiday shopping may sound rather obvious, but RSD co-founder Michael Kurtz says that, at first, he was opposed to the idea, which his wife came up with. “I was not on board with it,” he admits. “My initial response at the time was, ‘Ah, that’s for big-box stores and selling cheap toasters and stuff.’” But eventually, he came around, thinking they could do “a little bit smaller version” for the holidays. RSD Black Friday does feature fewer releases overall, but its main goal is to get customers through the door. “Most record stores do about two months’ worth of business” that day, Kurtz says. For Black Friday, Kurtz says what you’ll find in the racks is largely thanks to what he calls a “Secret Squirrel group” of about 20 record store owners nationwide, who help winnow down the overwhelming numbers of releases pitched by artists and record labels. “They’ve been around forever; they run iconic record stores,” Kurtz explains of this crate-digging cabal. “And I go to them and say, ‘Hey, do you think record stores would want to have this?’ Because Black Friday is not the same as Record Store Day. It’s not supposed to be just a limited thing only. It’s also supposed to be things that record stores want to have in their bins year-round.” But what’s true for both events is that they feature releases from a dizzying array of artists across multiple genres. That big tent approach, Kurtz reveals, was inspired by Metallica bassist Robert Trujillo, who early on convinced Kurtz to do a vinyl release by iconic jazz bassist Jaco Pastorius. “It went to No. 1 on Billboard‘s jazz chart,” Kurtz recalls. “And that made us rethink: ‘Oh, geez, we could do jazz records, we could do bluegrass records, we could do soul records, R&B, funk.” Of course, rock in its various forms is still a huge focus of both Record Store Day and RSD Black Friday, but in recent years, pop artists have climbed on board the vinyl train en masse, resulting in a surprising boom in customers who are too young to even remember a world where vinyl was once the only option. Kurtz says, “The majority of people who come to Record Store Day now and participate are younger than the age of 35, and slightly more female than male.” Of course, you can credit the biggest pop star in the world for that. While Kurtz says Billie Eilish’s 7-inch releases for RSD “sort of cracked the door open” for that demographic, he notes, “It got blown wide open with Taylor Swift. When she did her ‘Long Pond Studio Sessions’ record with us exclusively for record stores [in 2023], it changed everything.” That album became the first Record Store Day exclusive release ever to hit the top 10 of theBillboard200, proving that brand-new releases on vinyl could do just as well as streaming titles. For RSD Black Friday 2026, Kurtz predicts that it’ll be Noah Kahan ’s vinyls getting the youth through the door. “He’s got a special 7-inch that was done just for record stores that’s very very cool: It’s tied in with the ‘Hunger Games’ soundtrack,” says Kurtz, referring to “ Draw You Out, ” Kahan’s contribution to “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping – The Album.” “And then he’s also got an additional record that’ll be highly sought after. ” That would be “ The Last of the Bugs, ” which collects the four tracks Kahan added to the expanded edition of his album”The Great Divide.” Kurtz is also excited about a Bruce Springsteen live box set, the American version of The Beatles ’ Rubber Soul LP on gold vinyl, a live album by Billy Joel, a disc of the Doors ’ studio sessions and a 2-LP set by Ween “for all the pot smokers out there.” He also predicts the Miles Davis , Jerry Garcia Band and Grateful Dead releases will be popular, as well as the original, previously unreleased version of Joan Jett’s “ I Love Rock & Roll ” album and not one but three albums by Japanese guitar virtuoso Masayoshi Takanaka . Kurtz says he doesn’t even mind that many of those younger customers are buying vinyl not to play, but to display. “Y’know, I was originally freaked out about that because I’m a music person, but I kind of get it,” he tells me. “Like, I will get the Beatles’ ‘Rubber Soul’ reissue this year and I probably will never open it. I just want it because it’s so beautiful, and to know that I have one of 15,000 copies that will ever be printed … I want to keep it pristine.” Despite admitting to being “completely anxiety-ridden” each year over how successful each Record Store Day event will be, Kurtz is looking forward to the event’s 20th anniversary next year. He and co-founder Carrie Colliton would love to mark the milestone with live performances and some kind of art installation featuring past Record Store Day releases. (A copy of each of those limited releases is currently stored in a warehouse in Raleigh, North Carolina, in case you might want to pull off the vinyl equivalent of robbing Fort Knox.) But for right now, Kurtz notes, those plans are “dreams right now. They’re not reality.” Still, the failure he fears is unlikely. Nearly 20 years into an event which has helped drive pop culture back to the vinyl age, Kurtz says there’s no sign of its popularity tapering off. As he notes, “demand for [vinyl] and the excitement around it is completely still there – even more so, I think.” But, he acknowledges, “The only thing that’s a bit alarming is how expensive it’s becoming” – a reflection of the rising cost of shipping due to increases in gas and diesel. “It’s stunning for me as a person who’s ridden this tiger called Record Store Day for almost 20 years to see it from the beginning: When we first started we were the only ones doing new vinyl, and in the used bins you could find [high quality copies of] Led Zeppelin or the Beatles or Pink Floyd for $3, $5 — those days are over.” Related Stories Chris Pratt to Star in Sci-Fi Family Drama 'The Traveler,' Inks First-Look Producing Deal at Paramount (EXCLUSIVE) Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' Comeback: A Smaller $5 Million Salary, Optimistic Theater Owners and More Kurtz says it was interesting working with shops in the early days, and still can be today — because they’re independent in all sorts of ways, including what they prefer to emphasize in their stores and sometimes think RSD should focus on as a whole. “The most difficult thing about putting it together was working with record store owners, because they’re a very creative bunch,” he says. “They’re very different; they’re not people who typically play by the rules. They like to do things their way. So to try to get them all together to do this was very difficult.” He adds, “I was in London once and there was a record store owner who just just raked me over the coals because we’d done the Taylor Swift record. I was like, ‘What records do you like?’ He’s like, ‘Yes, Black Sabbath, Deep Purple …’ and I said, ‘OK I get it. That’s what you love and what you’re passionate about, but there’s another generation.’ And so it’s working with them and not alienating them, because sometimes I do that by accident.” New ‘Rocky’ Book Celebrates 50th Anniversary With Rare and Never-Seen-Before Paintings Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie Settle Winery Lawsuit That Revealed Abuse Allegations Indie Filmmakers at WAVES Film Bazaar Look to ‘Dangal’ China Playbook, Pop-Up Cinemas and Screening Fees to Find Audiences India Targets at Least 10 Million AI Workers Through National AI Talent Mission, WAVES Film Bazaar Panel Hears ‘The Hawk’ Starring Will Ferrell Canceled After One Season at Netflix U2 Salutes Dolly Parton With Recreation of Their ‘Torn’ Duet in NFL Thanksgiving Eve Halftime Show Loading comments...

full_text: × Nov 26, 2026 8:22am PT Mark Tildesley, Production Designer on ‘No Time to Die,’ ‘28 Days Later’ and Upcoming Beatles Biopics, Dies at 63 By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest Mark Tildesley, Production Designer on ‘No Time to Die,’ ‘28 Days Later’ and Upcoming Beatles Biopics, Dies at 63 2 hours ago Danny Boyle Backs Jack O’Connell as a Bond Villain, but Says He ‘Would Have Been Great’ as 007 4 hours ago Huw Edwards Speaks Publicly About Conviction and Downfall for First Time in Channel 4 Doc: ‘I’d Lost the Plot’ 7 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Mark Tildesley , the acclaimed British production designer who worked on major titles including the most recent James Bond movie “ No Time to Die ,” has died. He was 63. Tildesley is understood to have passed away on Nov. 24 following a long illness. Across a career spanning more than 30 years, Tildesley collaborated with an array of leading directors both in the U.K. and beyond, on titles ranging from smaller indie films to big-budget Hollywood productions. Among those he worked with were Danny Boyle , Richard Curtis, Michael Winterbottom, Martin McDonagh, Mike Leigh, Paul Thomas Anderson, Cary Joji Fukunaga, Ron Howard, Ben Wheatley, Oliver Stone and Sam Mendes . Related Stories Chris Pratt to Star in Sci-Fi Family Drama 'The Traveler,' Inks First-Look Producing Deal at Paramount (EXCLUSIVE) Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' Comeback: A Smaller $5 Million Salary, Optimistic Theater Owners and More Winterbottom would become a seven-time collaborator, with Tildesley working with the director almost back-to-back in the late 1990s and early 2000s on films such as “I Want You,” “Wonderland,” “The Claim,” “24 Hour Party People” and “Code 46.” Tildesley first joined forces with Boyle on his 2002 groundbreaking zombie hit “28 Days Later,” but the two would team up again on films including “Millions,” “Sunshine,” “Trance” and “T2 Trainspotting.” Boyle also tapped Tildesley as his designer alongside Suttirat Anne Larlarb for the 2012 London Olympics opening ceremony, a four-hour, wildly acclaimed extravaganza. It would win Boyle, Larlarb and Tildesley the Emmy for outstanding art direction for variety or nonfiction programming. With Mendes, he served as production designer on both “Empire of Light” and the upcoming “The Beatles — A Four-Film Cinematic Event” alongside Stefania Cella and Neal Callow. “Mark was a one-off: gentle, funny, warm, mischievous, entirely original and extraordinarily gifted,” said Mendes. “My abiding memory of him is from ‘Empire of Light,’ flying down the Margate seafront on a motorised scooter, his technicolored scarf flapping in the wind, twinkling like a schoolboy playing hooky. A unique spirit and a wonderful artist. I am one of hundreds of people who are desperately sad that he is gone.” Other credits include Leigh’s “Happy-Go-Lucky,” Curtis’ “The Boat that Rocked,” Lone Scherfig’s “One Day,” Bill Condon’s “The Fifth Estate,” Wheatley’s “High-Rise” and McDonagh’s “The Banshees of Inisherin.” With Fernando Meirelles he teamed on both “The Constant Gardener” and “The Two Popes.” Tildesley’s most recent credits were Noah Baumbach’s “Jay Kelly” and Joseph Kosinski’s “F1: The Movie.” “We are very sad to hear the news of Mark’s death,” said the British Film Designers Guild (BFDG), which awarded Tildesley three times (for “High-Rise,” “Empire of Light” and “F1: The Movie”). “Besides being a well-respected and extremely talented production designer, he was a friend and colleague to many of our members and will be very much missed by everyone in the Industry who knew and worked with him.” Former Disney Boss Bob Iger ‘Got ABC Employee Pregnant’ During Affair, New Book Claims Microdrama Revenue to Hit $20 Billion in 2026, but Profits Outside China Remain Thin, Media Partners Asia Report Finds Qatar Is Forging Ahead With Film and TV Industry Plan, Undeterred by Regional Turbulence Ivory Coast’s SICA Market Looks to Turn Africa’s Creative Talent Into Economic Opportunity Ariana Grande Says ‘Petal’ Music Video Backlash Felt Like ‘Black Mirror’ and ‘I Wouldn’t Change a Thing. title: Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Leads With $15 Million on Thanksgiving Eve, ‘Focker In-Law’ Earns $5 Million on Opening Day
full_text: × Nov 26, 2026 8:11am PT Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Leads With $15 Million on Thanksgiving Eve, ‘Focker In-Law’ Earns $5 Million on Opening Day By Rebecca Rubin Plus Icon Rebecca Rubin Senior Film and Media Reporter rebeccaarubin Latest Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Leads With $15 Million on Thanksgiving Eve, ‘Focker In-Law’ Earns $5 Million on Opening Day 2 hours ago ‘Focker In-Law’ Director on Casting Ariana Grande, Why Barbra Streisand and Dustin Hoffman Didn’t Return and What the Ending Means for Another Sequel 22 hours ago Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Scores $16 Million on Tuesday, ‘Hexed’ Earns $2 Million in Previews 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Murray Close/Lionsgate “Sunrise on the Reaping” stuffed the box office competition ahead of Thanksgiving, generating $15 million on Wednesday. Fueled by positive word-of-mouth, Lionsgate’s “Hunger Games” prequel looks to collect $85 million over the five-day holiday period, which would push its domestic tally to $233 million. Despite opening last weekend, “Sunrise on the Reaping” towering over two new releases. Disney’s animated “Hexed” earned $7.6 million from 3,725 theaters, and Universal’s comedy “Focker In-Law” grossed $5.3 million from 3,382 venues on their respective opening days. (“Focker In-Law” didn’t have Tuesday previews; showtimes began on Wednesday.) Although “Hexed” has pulled ahead on Wednesday charts, the fantasy adventure is projected to finish the weekend in third place behind “Focker In-Law.” Based on updated projections, “Hexed” is now targeting a five-day debut of $31 million to $35 million, while “Focker In-Law” is aiming for $35 million to $36 million over the same frame. Both films are falling short of pre-release expectations, which forecasted a $40 million to $45 million haul. Related Stories Chris Pratt to Star in Sci-Fi Family Drama 'The Traveler,' Inks First-Look Producing Deal at Paramount (EXCLUSIVE) Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' Comeback: A Smaller $5 Million Salary, Optimistic Theater Owners and More Elsewhere, Netflix’s Brad Pitt-led “The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” brought in $910,00 from 252 Imax screens on Wednesday. The sequel to Sony’s “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” which isn’t getting a traditional wide release, is expected to earn $4 million to $5 million by Sunday. In the case of “Hexed,” this opening weekend could spell trouble. That’s because the studio spent more than $200 million to produce the film, and theaters keep about half of ticket sales. So the studio needs the movie to resonate in international markets, and throughout holiday season, to justify the sizable prize tag. Disney has long dominated the Thanksgiving corridor, and the studio’s animated sequels, namely “Moana 2” and “Zootopia 2,” are some of the holiday’s biggest earners of all time. Post-pandemic, however, Disney has struggled with original offerings, including 2024’s “Wish” ($31 million over its first five days) and 2022’s “Strange World” ($18 million debut over its first five days). “Wish” tapped out with $254 million worldwide on a $200 million budget, while “Strange World” left theaters with $73 million globally on a $180 million budget. What’s promising in this case, though, is that audiences seem to like “Hexed,” which was awarded an “A-” grade on CinemaScore exit polls. Positive sentiment should help the film’s box office longevity. The story follows a teen girl who discovers magical powers that take her from suburbia to Hexe, the world of witches. “Focker In-Law” also carries a sizable budget; Universal and Paramount co-financed the film for $90 million. Although theatrical comedies have become a box office rarity, the three prior “Focker” movies were notable box office winners. The original comedy of errors, 2000’s “Meet the Parents,” starring Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro as mismatched in-laws Greg Focker and Jack Byrnes, generated $330 million worldwide. The 2004 sequel “Meet the Fockers” is the highest-grossing in the franchise with $522 million worldwide, while 2010’s “Little Fockers” amassed $310 million worldwide. In this installment, Ariana Grande joins in the festivities the girlfriend of Greg’s son Henry (Skyler Gisondo) who meets the family as they gather for Jack’s 80th birthday party. Critics panned the film (a 29% on Rotten Tomatoes) but moviegoers have been more receptive; “Focker In-Law” holds a “B+” grade on CinemaScore exit polls. Despite the range of offerings, this Thanksgiving will fall short of cementing any box office records. Ticket sales are expected to hit $210 million to $215 million across all films in the marketplace. Thanksgiving 2024 was the holiday’s biggest on record with $422 million across all films, led by “Moana 2″ ($225 million debut), “Wicked” ($118 million) and “Gladiator II” ($44 million). Last year was among the top five with $293 million, boosted by “Zootopia 2” and “Wicked: For Good.” Theater owners aren’t discouraged because domestic ticket sales are already 20% above the same point in 2025. Plus, North American revenues are projected to surpass $10 billion for the first time since Covid upended the theatrical business. The Oscar-winning director and post-production company Digital District will present the footage as they explain their method and tools for using AI on the film. Hazanavicius and his team turned to the technology for parts of the development and post-production stages, while the actual shoot used traditional sets and filming methods. The Third Hand stars François Civil as a French soldier who is wounded in battle in World War One, then wakes up in the laboratory of a mad scientist, who has grafted a German hand onto his abdomen. The case study will be followed by a discussion with David Cormand, Member of the European Parliament, on how Europe can regulate AI while protecting creators’ rights and cultural sovereignty. Hazanavicius is attending France ’s Alpine Les Arcs Film Festival this year as the Ambassador of its Talent Village which will see him share lessons from his career with the eight emerging directors. His last feature The Most Precious of Cargoes saw him direct animation for the first time. The AI case study is part of the conference program of the Les Arcs’ Industry Village. Other panels will include “Beyond Counting: Ten Years of Gender Equality Policies in European Cinema” and a European Producers Club discussion on the upcoming revision of the EU framework for audiovisual media services regulation and implications for the audiovisual sector. This follows the departures of Content Director Ulla Pors and Program Director Dorthe Thirstrup following the disastrous launch of Alle Elsker Rasmus ( Everybody Loves Rasmus ). Related Stories News Content Chiefs At Denmark's TV2 Step Down To "Restore Trust" After Backlash Over 'Truman Show'-Style Reality Series News Banijay Takes On Norway's 'The Comedy League' The show faced immense public backlash for duping comedian Rasmus Wallbridge into believing his dream film concept was being produced. It was scrapped soon after launch, and TV2’s directors have launched an investigation into how the show was greenlit in the first place. Their response has been fast and decisive during in an almost unprecedented situation for a major European broadcaster. Watch on Deadline Roland is a former TV2 exec, having risen as high as Head of Content, and returns after four years in the independent production sector. He had worked as Managing Director of Strong Productions, the Fremantle Denmark production house that merged with Blu last year. Following his exit there, he launched his own company, Shift Studios. Sune’s experience from both sides of the table will prove valuable in the time ahead.” Roland acknowledged he was joining in “particularly challenging times,” but added: TV2 holds a special place for me, and I know how many talented and dedicated people work every day to create content that truly matters to the Danish public. I look forward to contributing my experience and collaborating with both colleagues and production companies.” Roland worked as TV2’s Head of Factual between 2007 and 2011, and then from 2012 until 2022 held roles such as Head of Programming, Channel Head, and Head of Content. He has also held senior leadership positions at Koncern TV and Metronome Productions. title: BBC Under Investigation for Antisemitism Amid “Growing Feeling of Discomfort Among Jewish Staff”
full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All November 26, 2026 7:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The BBC building in central London. Courtesy of Getty The BBC is under investigation over allegations of “a hostile work environment” for Jewish employees. Lord John Mann, the government’s antisemitism adviser, told the broadcaster’s Today program on Thursday that he’s opening an investigation “because there seems to be a growing feeling of discomfort among Jewish staff,” adding: “Some of the things that I’m being told have been quite disturbing sometimes, how little the senior managers of the BBC seem to get it, and so I’m opening this up.” Mann encouraged any Jewish people currently working or who used to work for the corporation to come forward and talk to him. He expects to wrap up by Easter, at which point he’ll report back to the BBC. Related Stories Movies Get Ready for the Great Asterix Film Festival and Three Restored 'Asterix' Animated Movies! TV 'Dark' Creators Revisit Eerie German Forests in First 'Sonnental' Teaser In a statement, a BBC representative said the public broadcaster takes “any and all allegations of discrimination extremely seriously — there is no place for it at the BBC. We have introduced compulsory training on antisemitism for all our staff, and we actively encourage colleagues to report any incidences or concerns they have.” Concluded the statement: “We are determined to ensure the BBC is a place where everyone can be themselves and feel accepted.” Mann won’t be probing any department or program in particular, but said an “underlying atmosphere” hostile to Jewish members of staff. “The personal validations that I hear from former and current BBC Jewish employees and contractors is that, fundamentally, there is an institutional culture that demands that Jewish people must be expected to justify their existence, their identity, how they define their Jewishness,” he said. The adviser maintained he has “no agenda against the BBC” and said to Today : “Look, there is a problem. The question is — is the problem just a few people? Is it a problem that’s easily solved? But if it’s an institutional problem, that’s much deeper and more difficult to solve. It may be. I’ll report the facts.” The news of the investigation comes just a few weeks after an Oscar-winning producer, Lucie Kon, said she received a £400,000 ($525,000) payout from the BBC after alleging antisemitic remarks from her colleagues while she worked there. Kon, a commissioning editor on several documentaries at the broadcaster, including the Academy Award-winning Mr Nobody Against Putin , said at the time: “I really did feel like I had Jew stamped on my forehead. I became a problem.” The BBC did not uphold the claims of antisemitism, but accepted there were “shortcomings” in how Kon was treated, and didn’t go into further detail. Deputy director general Rhodri Talfan Davies said there are “very, very robust processes” that are reviewed regularly at a Broadcasting Press Guild lunch earlier this month. “Of course, in any large organisation there can be instances of discrimination, which you deal with when they arise, but there is no evidence of any systemic issue within the BBC that would merit anything like that,” said Davies. “I don’t believe there is institutional discrimination of any sort in the BBC, but I think as an organisation you always have to look harder and review how you go about identifying issues, and that work is never done.” THR

title: Get Ready for the Great Asterix Film Festival and Three Restored ‘Asterix’ Animated Movies!
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All November 26, 2026 6:59am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Asterix and Cleopatra' Courtesy of 1968 PRODUCTIONS DARGAUD FILMS/RENE GOSCINNY/ALBERT UDERZO StudioCanal , the studio unit of Canal+ Group , and Mediatoon Distribution, the content distribution arm of Média-Participations, have struck a European distribution agreement covering three restored animated Asterix film classics. The agreement covers three landmark titles from the franchise’s catalogue, namely Asterix the Gaul , Asterix and Cleopatra , and Asterix Conquers Rome , across several European territories, including France, Germany, Poland and the Netherlands. Financial terms weren’t disclosed. The first major initiative under the partnership will be The Great Asterix Film Festival organized by StudioCanal in Germany from January 2027. Related Stories TV 'Dark' Creators Revisit Eerie German Forests in First 'Sonnental' Teaser News French Court Rejects Depardieu Appeal in Rape Case “The festival will bring these three films back to the big screen in their restored versions, offering audiences a unique opportunity to rediscover some of the most iconic animated adventures of the famous Gaul,” the company said on Thursday. “Alongside the theatrical event, a collector’s DVD box set featuring the three films will be released in France and Germany during the 2026 holiday season and in the spring of 2027, respectively. In Poland and the Netherlands, the films will also become available on video-on-demand platforms, reaching new audiences across both territories.” The initiative forms part of a broader effort to celebrate and promote the Asterix universe across Europe. “It will accompany several important milestones in the history of the franchise over the coming years, including the 50th anniversary of Asterix Conquers Rome and the 60th anniversary of Asterix the Gaul in 2028,” StudioCanal said. With more than 400 million comic books sold worldwide and generations of readers and viewers captivated over the past six decades, Asterix , created by René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo , is one of Europe’s most successful and enduring cultural franchises. The collaboration also reflects StudioCanal’s long-standing commitment to the Asterix universe, owned by Les Editions Albert René, which holds all exploitation rights. “ Asterix is one of the most iconic works of European popular culture and continues to bring generations together,” said Pauline Saint-Hilaire, head of catalogue at StudioCanal. “Through this agreement with Mediatoon Distribution, we are delighted to help new audiences discover, or rediscover, these films in their restored versions and contribute to the lasting appeal of this unique universe.” Added Frédéric Gentet, head of sales at Mediatoon Distribution: “For generations, Asterix has brought together audiences of all ages. We are thrilled to join forces with StudioCanal’s to give these animated classics new visibility across Europe. From the Asterix Kino Festival to new digital launches and collector editions, we are celebrating the extraordinary heritage and timeless appeal of one of Europe’s most beloved brands.” THR
